overall: The AG found the Fire Chief Search Committee was a public body that violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post meeting notice and prepare minutes, rejected the Board's Connelly defense, found no Board violation, and ordered minutes creation and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Fire Chief Search Committee was a public body that met from April to July without complying with the Open Meeting Law. The Board argued the Connelly exception applied.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Connelly exception does not apply to the Committee.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee held meetings without posting notice as the Open Meeting Law requires.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee was a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and that it violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to post notice of its meetings

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee's meetings went forward without the minutes the Open Meeting Law requires being prepared.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee was a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and that it violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to post notice of its meetings or to prepare minutes of its meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint, to the extent it alleged the Lancaster Select Board itself violated the Open Meeting Law, was addressed in a footnote.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that the complaint alleges that the Lancaster Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law, we find that it did not.

remedy: Within 60 days of the letter, the Committee must create minutes for its meetings in accordance with the guidance in the letter and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
The Committee must create minutes for its past meetings to the best of its ability, using whatever means are available, including documents and the memories and notes of attendees.
If the Committee has been disbanded, the Select Board must create minutes of the Committee's meetings.
The Committee (and the Board, as applicable) must comply immediately and in the future with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee, within 60 days of the date of this letter, to create minutes for its meetings in accordance with the guidance herein and that it certify to our office that it has done so.
